checks.label: The moment of a force is the force × its distance normal to the force: each gauge lists weight × distance from the pivot for every weight on its side, and totals them

If an object is balanced, the total clockwise moment about a pivot equals the total anticlockwise moment: every bar drawn hangs level only when its totals match, and otherwise tips towards the bigger one unless a peg holds it

The distance from the pivot is measured at right angles to the line of the force: each weight hangs straight down, so its distance runs along the level bar from the pivot, and on a rule it is its mark less the pivot's mark
Each typed answer and slip is worked from the lesson's figures: 12 cm (33.3, 20), 80 cm (30, 57.5), 20 cm (40, 17.1), 4 N (9, 2.7, 1.3), 59 kN (50, 41), 4 N (2, 3, 6) and 0.8 m (7.2, 2.4)
With each typed answer in place and the peg out, every bar hangs level: the answers balance the moments
The choices follow the totals: 120 against 90 N cm tips the left side down once the peg is out, and 60 against 60 N cm stays level
Before an answer nothing gives it away: the unknown reads "?", and every gauge total reads "?"; after it, each shows its figure
A lower level hangs by one string, so the bar above feels it as one weight at its hook: folded it is one 6 N weight, and the top bar feels 6 × 20 = 120 N cm from it, folded or not
A bar's own weight acts at its middle: pivoted there it turns nothing, and pivoted 20 cm from the left end of the 60 cm, 2 N bar it makes 20 N cm, balancing the 1 N at that end
Every demonstration is over within 5 s of its screen opening and nothing moves during the 0.35 s screen fade; every answer's motion is over within 2.5 s
